markets.marketQuestion: Will Arbitrum announce a new TradFi chain partnership before Feb 2027?
markets.marketSource:
• Official Arbitrum Foundation and Offchain Labs communications (blog, X)

• Official communications from the TradFi partner

• Consensus of credible reports from reputable news organizations
markets.additionalInfo:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if, after the creation of this market and before January 31, 2027 – 00:00 PST, Arbitrum (the Arbitrum Foundation or Offchain Labs) or a new TradFi partner officially announces that the partner will build or launch its own dedicated blockchain using Arbitrum technology. 

Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

For the purposes of this market:

• A “TradFi partner” is a traditional financial institution or established financial services company, such as a bank, broker-dealer, asset manager, stock or derivatives exchange, payments company, insurer, or custodian.

• Robinhood and any chain partnership announced before the creation of this market do not qualify. Only new announcements made after market deployment are eligible.

• The announcement must be made through an official channel of Arbitrum, Offchain Labs, or the TradFi partner. A testnet launch or a stated plan to build qualifies, but rumors, reports without official confirmation, and non-chain integrations (e.g., tokenized assets deployed on the existing Arbitrum One network) do not qualify.

• Crypto-native companies and protocols (e.g., exchanges or DeFi projects without a traditional finance business) do not qualify as a TradFi partner.

markets.marketQuestion: Aave bad debt or exploit in October 2026?
markets.additionalInfo:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Aave protocol suffers a qualifying bad debt event or exploit at any time after the creation of this market and before November 1, 2026 - 00:00 UTC.

Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

For the purposes of this market:

• "Exploit" is defined as a hack, smart contract vulnerability exploit, oracle manipulation, or compromised key attack on any official Aave-governed deployment (e.g., Aave V2, V3, or V4 on any chain) resulting in a verifiable loss of $1,000,000 or more in a single incident.

• "Bad debt" is defined as unrecoverable debt on any official Aave deployment, where liquidated or undercollateralized positions leave the protocol with unpaid debt of $1,000,000 or more in a single incident, as confirmed by onchain data.

• Only incidents occurring after market creation are eligible. Incidents that began before market creation do not qualify.

• Losses must be realized and not covered in full by the protocol's own mechanisms within the same incident (e.g., Umbrella/Safety Module coverage does not negate qualifying bad debt, but recovery of exploited funds does not negate an exploit that has already occurred).

• Exploits of third-party protocols that merely integrate Aave, bridged or wrapped asset depegs without resulting protocol bad debt, and temporary price volatility or normal liquidations do not qualify.

markets.marketQuestion: Will there be a $1M+ hack this week?
markets.additionalInfo:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if a smart contract/program, set of related smart contracts/programs, crypto project, crypto business, or crypto service suffers from a hack/exploit totalling $1,000,000 or more, at anytime between the initiation date of this market and exactly 7 days later.

Otherwise this market will resolve to “No.”

For the purposes of this market, the loss of funds must be verifiable onchain.
Compromised private keys (leading to loss of funds) will count under a “hack” for the purposes of this market, as long as the loss is provably verifiable onchain.

Oracle manipulation/misconfigurations leading to loss of funds count under a “hack.”
The value exploited must total $1,000,000 or more in a single incident to qualify for a “Yes” outcome.

The value of an exploit is measured by the realized loss incurred by users or the protocol(s) affected as a result of the incident. Unrealized losses by protocols or users do not count towards the measurable value of the exploit.
